issue_paraphrase: When an application enables chunked transfer encoding on a response (a common pattern for streaming output, done by setting a Transfer-Encoding header) and then sends a body string, Express also writes a Content-Length header on the same response. HTTP forbids the two headers from appearing together, and both browsers and Node's own HTTP client reject such a response outright with a parse error like "Content-Length can't be present with Transfer-Encoding", so the client never receives the payload. Express should only add Content-Length when the response does not already declare a Transfer-Encoding header.
fix_summary: In res.send(), only populate Content-Length when the response does not already carry a Transfer-Encoding header; added a 4-case regression test (chunked/compress/deflate/gzip).
notes: JavaScript, express 5.2.1 at HEAD of master (2026-06 era). No runtime network. Golden group runs in ~25ms. Direct repro needs supertest (devDependency, installed by npm install). Node >= 18 is required (node-22 image satisfies).

reproduction: cd <repo> && npm install && node -e "var supertest = require('supertest'); var express = require('./'); var app = express(); app.use(function (req, res) { res.clearCookie('sid', { path: '/admin', maxAge: 1000 }).end(); }); supertest(app).get('/').end(function (err, res) { if (err) { console.log('FAIL:', err.message); process.exit(1); } console.log(res.headers['set-cookie']); });" -- or: ./node_modules/.bin/mocha --require test/support/env -g "should ignore" test/res.clearCookie.js
observed_failure_at_parent: Set-Cookie header is 'sid=; Max-Age=1; Path=/admin; Expires=Fri, 11 Sep 2026 05:44:15 GMT' (a future expiry - the cookie is not cleared, and with Max-Age present the browser keeps it); mocha: 'should ignore maxAge' and 'should ignore user supplied expires param' both fail - expected Set-Cookie 'sid=; Path=/admin; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT', got a Max-Age/future-Expires variant (for the expires-param test it got the caller's future date 'Fri, 11 Sep 2026 ...' instead of 1970)
verified: both directions observed in a bench-base:node-22 container at /tmp/express (express 5.0.0-beta.3 era). PARENT 160b91cb: git reset --hard + git clean -fd, sed proves res.clearCookie body is 'var opts = merge({ expires: new Date(1), path: '/' }, options);' with no maxAge/expires stripping; direct repro prints the Max-Age=1 future-expiry cookie (script exits 2); mocha group 0 passing / 2 failing. FIX 82fc12a4: sed proves 'const opts = { path: '/', ...options, expires: new Date(1)}; delete opts.maxAge'; direct repro prints 'sid=; Path=/admin; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT'; same mocha group 2 passing.
install_recipe: cd <repo> && npm install --no-audit --no-fund  (installs runtime deps plus mocha/supertest from devDependencies)
issue_paraphrase: The cookie-clearing helper accepts the same options object as cookie setting, so a caller can pass maxAge or an explicit expires date, and those values win over the forced immediate deletion: clearing a cookie with a keep-alive maxAge emits a Set-Cookie header carrying Max-Age plus a future Expires timestamp, and passing an expires date emits that future date instead of a past one. In both cases the cookie survives (or is re-created for a short lifetime) instead of being removed, so a session or preference the application tried to delete keeps coming back.
fix_summary: res.clearCookie now builds options as { path: '/', ...options, expires: past } and explicitly deletes opts.maxAge before calling this.cookie, so user-supplied expiry options can never postpone the forced expiration.
notes: JavaScript, express 5.0.0-beta.3 era (2024-08). No runtime network. Golden group runs in ~18ms. issue_paraphrase: The helper that sets a redirect target only accepts plain strings: passing any other value that describes a URL, such as a WHATWG URL object created with the global URL constructor, makes the whole request fail. Instead of issuing a redirect, the server answers with an internal error (HTTP 500) and no Location header, so any code that builds redirect locations programmatically with URL objects (or other non-string values) is silently broken. Non-string location values should be converted to their string form and then handled like any other URL.
fix_summary: res.location converts its argument with String(url) before the 'back' alias check and encoding/parsing steps, so URL instances and other coercible values work.
notes: JavaScript, express 4.19.0 era (2024-03). No runtime network. Golden test runs in ~16ms. This tree's package.json differs from master (4.x deps: path-to-regexp, methods, array-flatten, utils-merge...), so install node_modules while checked out at this commit. The added test is guarded by 'typeof URL !== undefined' which is always true on node-22.

issue_paraphrase: Setting the response status code to an invalid value is silently accepted: codes below 100 or above 999, non-integers like 200.1, a numeric string such as "200", NaN, or undefined are all stored as the response status without complaint. The request then completes with a wrong, unparseable, or meaningless status line - clients observe e.g. 200 OK where an error was intended - instead of failing immediately with a clear message. Invalid status codes should be rejected with an explicit error as soon as they are set.
fix_summary: res.status now validates its argument: throws a TypeError for anything that is not an integer and a RangeError for integers outside 100-999, before assigning statusCode; test/res.sendStatus.js also gained an invalid-code regression test (behavior inherited via res.sendStatus -> res.status).
notes: JavaScript, express 5.0.0-beta.3 era (2024-07). No runtime network.
